steps.text: In a large pot with boiling salted water cook egg noodles until al dente. Drain.
In a large bowl mix together the sour cream, 1/4 cup of the grated Parmesan cheese, chives, salt, ground black pepper, and garlic.
Stir in butter or margarine to hot egg noodles. Stir in sour cream mixture.
Arrange noodles on warm platter and sprinkle with remaining 1/4 cup of grated Parmesan cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Noodles Romanoff II
raw_recipe.description: Sour cream and Parmesan cheese give a tart edge to the creaminess of this egg noodle dish. Chopped chives and a clove of garlic add sparks of color and an earthy tone. Serve hot with more Parmesan sprinkled over the top.
raw_recipe.name: Noodles Romanoff II

review.reviewBody: I messed with this recipe a bit. Used 1 cup of Parmesean, 2/3 cup of sour cream, half the salt, and 6 oz of noodles. We liked it a lot like that. We ate it all for supper-no leftovers. I agree with the first reviewer-way to much sour cream-but if you love the sour cream flavor you'd like the original recipe.

I pretty much tweaked the heck out of the recipe. ✓ Do NOT use "reduced fat" or "skim" sour cream if you absolutely have to use sour cream. I much prefer Creme Fraiche. ✓ Use MUCH less whole sour cream/Creme Fraiche. More like a half of a cup. Definitely NOT two cups! That's WAY too much! Your mixture should actually be chunky with Romano/Parmesan Cheese when you mix it, NOT smooth; ✓ Use GRATED Romano/Parmesan Cheese Blend, NOT just Parmesan. That's NOT Noodles Romanoff. It's Noodles Parmesiano. The kind in the bottle works BETTER in my experience, for both Noodles Romanoff and Noodles Parmesiano than freshly grated; ✓ Fresh Chopped Parsley (adds color and cuts garlic breath); ✓ Paprika (the common variety will do fine). It adds color and, combined with Romano Cheese, is what makes "Noodles Romanoff" Noodles Romanoff; ✓ NO Onion (it doesn't work well with the dish, IMO. The Paprika and Romano Cheese are what give the dish it's special "zing"; ✓ COARSE Ground WHITE Pepper for Pepper with a VERY Minimal amount of MEDIUM Ground BLACK Pepper; ✓ Garlic Powder VERY Sparingly. NO chopped or minced cloves as they break the smooth texture of the sauce AND overpower the delicate flavor; ✓ I do NOT add salt to the Romanoff mixture as I "salt like the sea" any noodles that I cook with Diamond Kosher Salt and I do NOT rinse the noodles, only drain but NOT COMPLETELY. The pasta water, a bit left in the noodles, helps to make the Romanoff sauce thick and velvety; ✓ No additional cheese is required if the Romanoff mixture is well done; ✓ Use high fat unsalted butter or ghee to butter the noodles. In the United States the quality (fat content) of butter is usually inferior so I prefer ghee. Be sparing. The goal is to make sure that the noodles don't stick together but you don't want so much that the Romanoff mixture slips off. My recipe came out absolutely perfect! It was great next day as well and I just added a splash of Whole Milk to it to facilitate reheating.

Everyone really love this and even came back for seconds or thirds. Even those people who are trying to keep their carbohydrates low. I didn't have any chives so I used the green part of a couple of green onions, sliced thinly. I only used a cup and a half of sour cream but I also used less noodles. Then I mixed the sauce in a little at a time until I felt that the mixture was creamy enough. My mother saved the remainder of the sauce for a salad dressing.

I made this using angel hair pasta and a little less sour cream (I used fat free sour cream). Garlic powder gave it the rich flavor. I served this with teriyaki chicken and steamed broccoli, but you could easily make a meal out of this by adding some clams or cooked shrimp. Very delicious!
Altering this a ton...no sour cream...using cream cheese...adding broccoli roasted with olive oil and garlic. Next may add chicken too.

Wow, I thought this recipe was phenomenal! I halved the recipe and only adjusted the ingredients by adding extra black pepper because I love pepper! I decided to pre-make the sauce because I wanted to prep dinner as much as possible. Maybe allowing the flavors to marry is what made this so good. I absolutely will make this again and again!

I wanted to make something quick and easy and selected this one. I was out of chives so I used parsley and I like to spice things up a bit so I added about 1/2 teaspoon of crushed red pepper flakes. Next time I would like to use chives and warm the sour cream and cheese mixture up before adding the noodles. I liked it overall. Nice and quick to make.
Too much sour cream flavor, and doesn't really have the oomph that I remember from when I had it years ago.
per reviews, i used half the sour cream called for. this reminds me so much of the old betty crocker noodles romanoff mix. sure hated when they stopped making it. i've made this again and again.

Really excellent. Instead of wide egg noodles, I used rainbow rotini noodles and the bowl was scraped clean. My kids declared it was one of the best things I had ever cooked and my husband went up for 3rds. I know I'll be making this again.
WAY to much sour cream. thats all you can taste. only do half of the amount.
I cut the portions in half since I only cook for two! It came out so delish!
Loved these. They are such a great accompaniment with so many entrees. Will be making these again and again.
This recipe doesn't do justice to the ingredients, I think.
A bit bland and too much sour cream taste
This isn't quite like my childhood favorite so the second time I made this I used Romano cheese and it was perfect! My new comfort food!
Excellent and amazingly easy!
I put some pine nuts in it and used it as the main course for a meatless meal. It was incredible!
I used Balkan Yogourt in place of the Sour Cream. Pretty good...not Great...just good.
I think less sour cream would've made it better. Maybe a bit more garlic
